newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain government blames ETA for killing Basque man.
newsitem.headline: Spain government blames ETA for killing Basque man.

text.p: The Spanish government blamed the separatist group ETA on Friday for killing a Basque bicycle merchant and said the group was trying to terrorise the Basque people.

Spanish newspapers said ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) may have targeted Eugenio Olaciregi, 39, on suspicion he made a call to police that led to the arrest of one of the group's activists last March.
An unidentified gunman shot Olaciregi in the back of a head with a pistol on Thursday afternoon in the Basque town of San Sebastian. He was on his way to work in a nearby bicycle shop.
"ETA is trying to make society live in fear," Basque regional government President Jose Antonio Ardanza told reporters on Friday.
No arrests have been made in the case.
Spanish newspapers quoted police sources as saying ETA activist Valentin Lasarte was arrested in March 1996 hours after he bought a bike at the shop where Olaciregi worked.

However, Basque officials said on Friday they could not confirm Olaciregi was the person who made the anonymous phone call that led to the arrest of Lasarte and noted that other people could have spotted him in the area on that day.

"It seems the reason the terrorists' had for the murder yesterday is that (the victim) was a worker who was Basque and lived in the Basque country," government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told reporters in Madrid after the weekly cabinet meeting on Friday.
ETA has killed about 800 people in its drive for independence from Spain that began in 1968.
The group is also suspected in the January 8 attack on a Spanish army officer, shot dead by a woman in Madrid.
ETA frequently targets members of Spanish security forces. But Basque government officials said on Thursday Olaciregi had no connection to security forces.
